Reporting network regression and test results

Source: R/model_regression.R, R/model_results.R, R/model_tests.R, and 1 more
results.Rd

print() shows the result of estimate_mrqap() or of a test as a report: how the null distribution was made, the estimates, and the permutation p-values.

tidy() and glance() return the same results as a tibble, after {broom}. tidy() gives one row for each term of a model, and glance() gives one row for the whole model. They cover:

  • netreg, netreg_lm, netreg_glm, and netreg_css, from estimate_mrqap()

  • network_test, from test_random(), test_configuration(), and test_permutation()

  • netlm and netlogit, from net_regression() in {migraph}

  • ergm, from ergm() in {ergm}

  • sienaFit, from siena07() in {RSiena}

So an MRQAP result can sit in one table beside an ERGM or a SIENA one.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'netreg_lm'
print(x, ..., print_b = FALSE, print_random = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_glm'
print(x, ..., print_b = FALSE, print_random = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
tidy(
  x,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "less", "greater"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_lm'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_glm'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_css'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'network_test'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'network_test'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, exponentiate = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ergm'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, exponentiate = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ergm'
glance(x, deviance = FALSE, mcmc = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sienaFit'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sienaFit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'network_test'
print(x, ..., max.length = 6, digits = 3)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_css'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A model or test result, e.g. a netreg object, as returned by estimate_mrqap(), or a network_test object, as returned by test_random(), test_configuration(), or test_permutation().

...

Further arguments, passed to summary() for an ergm and otherwise not used.

print_b

Logical; also print coefficient-based (not t-based) permutation p-values.

print_random

Logical; print random intercepts when present.

exponentiate

Logical, whether to exponentiate the estimates, e.g. to give odds ratios for a logistic model.

alternative

For a netreg, which permutation p-value to report: "two.sided" (the default) for Pr(>=|t|), "less" for Pr(<=t), or "greater" for Pr(>=t).

conf.int

Logical, whether to add the columns conf.low and conf.high.

conf.level

The level of the interval that conf.int adds.

deviance, mcmc

For an ergm, whether to add the deviance columns or the MCMC settings.

max.length, digits

Not used.

Value

print() returns x, invisibly. tidy() and glance() return a tibble. tidy() gives the columns term, estimate, statistic, and p.value for a regression. For a netreg, it also adds the columns of the fit's term table, fit$terms: the effect (the formula term) each coefficient comes from, its layer, attribute, category, and reference category, and for an interaction its operands. These group the coefficients without parsing their names. and glance() gives the fit statistics that the model keeps. For a network_test, both give one row with the observed statistic, the mean and standard deviation of the null distribution, and the share of the null distribution at or below (p.lower) and at or above (p.upper) the observed statistic.

Details

A permutation test gives a p-value but no standard error, so the tidied regression results have no std.error column. For a netreg, p.value is read from the permutations of the test statistic, as print() shows it. When the predictors are permuted, the intercept has no test, and its p.value is NA.

For a {migraph} result, conf.int = TRUE adds the quantiles of the permuted test statistics. These describe the null distribution, not an interval around the estimate.

See also

Other models: control_mrqap(), regression, specify, tests

Examples

css_model <- estimate_mrqap(advice ~ same(dept) + reports,
                            manynet::ison_hightech, times = 5)
print(css_model, print_b = TRUE)
